name: Egypt
genZNote: Egypt built the Great Pyramid of Giza over 4,500 years ago and it's still the only surviving Ancient Wonder of the World — the Nile literally created a civilization so advanced, so early, that modern engineers still study how they pulled it off.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: Located in northeastern Africa (with the Sinai Peninsula extending into Asia), making it a transcontinental country bridging Africa and the Middle East.
Dominated by the Nile River, whose narrow fertile valley and delta support the overwhelming majority of Egypt's population amid otherwise vast desert.
Home to the Suez Canal, one of the world's most strategically vital shipping routes connecting the Mediterranean and Red Seas.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: Arabic is the official language; the culture blends ancient Pharaonic heritage with a predominantly Muslim, Arab identity and a significant Coptic Christian minority.
Home to some of the world's most iconic ancient monuments, including the Pyramids of Giza, the Sphinx, and the temples of Luxor and Karnak.
Cairo is one of the largest and most historically significant cities in the Arab and African worlds, a longstanding centre of Islamic scholarship (Al-Azhar University).

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A presidential republic with a President as head of state and government, alongside an elected House of Representatives.
One of the world's oldest continuous civilizations, with a documented history spanning over 5,000 years through Ancient Egyptian dynasties.
Experienced major political upheaval during the 2011 Arab Spring uprising, which led to significant political transitions in the years following.

sections.heading: 🧬 Medical & Scientific Developments
bullets: Ancient Egyptian civilization made foundational contributions to early medicine, surgery, mathematics, and monumental engineering.
Home to significant modern archaeological and Egyptology research, alongside a growing university and scientific research base.
The Grand Egyptian Museum, one of the world's largest archaeological museums, reflects major state investment in heritage and tourism-linked science.

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: Controls the Suez Canal, one of the world's most economically and strategically vital waterways for global maritime trade.
A founding member of the Arab League and a significant diplomatic power in Middle Eastern and North African affairs.
Maintains a long-standing peace treaty with Israel (1979), the first Arab state to do so, and plays an active mediating role in regional conflicts, particularly involving Gaza.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: India and Egypt share a 'Strategic Partnership' with historically deep ties dating to the Non-Aligned Movement, co-founded by Egypt's Gamal Abdel Nasser and India's Jawaharlal Nehru.
Growing trade and defence cooperation, alongside increased Indian investment following Egypt's economic liberalisation efforts.
The Suez Canal is strategically vital for Indian trade with Europe, making Egypt an important logistics and maritime partner.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: An economy driven significantly by tourism (built on its ancient heritage sites), Suez Canal transit revenues, remittances, and natural gas.
Agriculture along the Nile remains historically and economically significant, alongside a growing manufacturing and textile sector.
Faces ongoing economic reform challenges, including currency stabilisation and reducing public debt.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: The Pyramids of Giza — the only surviving Ancient Wonder of the World — and the Sphinx.
The Suez Canal, a globally critical shipping route.
Being one of the world's oldest continuous civilizations.
Co-founding the Non-Aligned Movement alongside India.

sections.heading: 💰 Currency & Economy
bullets: Currency: Egyptian Pound (EGP).
Economy driven by the Suez Canal (a critical global shipping route), tourism, agriculture along the Nile, and natural gas.
One of the largest economies in Africa and the Arab world.

sections.heading: 🌿 Ecology & Environment
bullets: Dominated by desert, with the Nile River and its delta supporting the vast majority of the population.
The Red Sea coast hosts globally significant coral reefs and diving ecosystems.

sections.heading: 📜 History & Major Turning Points
bullets: Home to one of the world's oldest civilizations, with a continuous history spanning over 5,000 years.
Came under British influence in the 19th century before gaining full independence in 1952 following a military coup.
President Gamal Abdel Nasser nationalized the Suez Canal in 1956, a defining moment of post-colonial assertion.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Major Political & Constitutional Changes
bullets: 1952 revolution ended the monarchy and established a republic.
The 2011 Arab Spring protests led to the ouster of longtime President Hosni Mubarak; a new constitutional order followed in subsequent years.

sections.heading: 🚀 Space, Innovation & Modern Development
bullets: Egyptian Space Agency coordinates satellite and space-research programmes.
Home to major archaeological-preservation technology efforts, including 3D-scanning of ancient monuments.

sections.heading: 🏅 Sports, Arts & Global Recognition
bullets: Football is the most popular sport, with a historically dominant national and club record in Africa.
The Pyramids of Giza and the Sphinx are among the most recognisable ancient monuments in the world.
Cairo is a major centre of Arabic film, music, and literature.

sections.heading: 🌐 International Organizations & Important Memberships
bullets: Founding member of the Arab League and the African Union.
Member of the UN and the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation; controls the strategically vital Suez Canal.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Egypt is a transcontinental presidential republic in northeastern Africa, home to one of the world's oldest civilizations and the strategically vital Suez Canal.
keyFacts: Presidential republic; major political transition following the 2011 Arab Spring.
Home to the Pyramids of Giza, the only surviving Ancient Wonder of the World.
Controls the Suez Canal, a critical global shipping route.
commonConfusion: Egypt is transcontinental — its Sinai Peninsula lies in Asia, while the rest of the country is in Africa — making it a bridge between the two continents.

highYieldFacts: Egypt: presidential republic, capital Cairo, controls the strategically vital Suez Canal.
Co-founded the Non-Aligned Movement with India (Nasser-Nehru).
First Arab state to sign a peace treaty with Israel (1979).
commonTraps: Assuming Egypt is entirely within Africa — the Sinai Peninsula lies in Asia.
Confusing the Suez Canal (Egypt) with the Panama Canal — different oceans, different continents connected.
mustRemember: Egypt: ancient civilization, Suez Canal controller, Non-Aligned Movement co-founder with India, first Arab-Israel peace treaty (1979).
